newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAB hit by strike, no impact on production.
newsitem.headline: SAB hit by strike, no impact on production.

text.p: A wage strike by workers at South African Breweries began on Monday but so far action has been muted and not hit production, a company spokesman said.

"It apppears the strike has had very half-hearted support and production has not been affected at all. A number of sites have not been affected by the strike. There is not site that has been 100 percent affected," breweries spokesman Adrian Botha told Reuters.
He declined to say how many workers from the 5,540-strong workforce had gone on strike.
"Gauging from the low level of support the strike received today (Monday) we hope it will not go on too long," he said.

The breweries' Beer Division said in a statement the company had offered workers a 10 percent wage deal. The wage package guaranteed a minimum monthly wage of 2,802 rand excluding allowances and bonuses.

The protracted wage negotiations had caused a long delay in the payment of increases and this had now prompted SAB to implement the wage increase after negotiations had been exhausted, the company said.
The wage offer had been implemented after deadlock at the end of three months of talks. Weekly-paid staff, comprising 73 percent of the bargaining unit, received a 10 percent increase.
Monthly-paid staff, who are on a performance related pay scheme, received an average 10 percent increase, with worst performers getting only 6.5 percent and the top performers a 16 percent increase.
The Food and Allied Workers' Union is demanding an 11.5 percent increase. Union spokesmen could immediately be reached for comment.
Union official Victor Nzuza told a local radio station the company had acted in bad faith by implementing the wage increase unilaterally and had undermined the union by its action.
